remit: fade statistically or fundamentally stretched market moves when reversal conditions exist
stance_summary: The Sep-16 25bp hike was already >90% priced; the 1-month US 2Y squeeze to a 1y extreme and the leftover SR3 hike path are the crowded energy-hawk overlay. Fade that overlay by receiving Mar-27 SOFR now that the overnight fixing has jumped and the oil-supply tail has been reduced—not because a z-score exists, but because the event is delivered and the additive hawkish narrative is weakening.

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Long duration / receive SOFR_2027-03 (CME SR3H7): packet implied_rate 4.58, price 95.42, +73bp versus NY Fed SOFR 3.85 as of 2026-09-17. This owns the leftover 1H27 hike premium after the delivered Sep FOMC. Alternative rates construction considered and rejected as inferior: pay CORRA vs receive SOFR to fade CA-US 2Y at -140bp (4th percentile 1y/5y), because the 156bp overnight CORRA-SOFR gap is an economic anchor, not an overshoot.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Short USDCAD (ECB cross spot 1.4010471204188482 as of 2026-09-18; 74th percentile 1y, 87th percentile 5y, +1.74% 1m). This is the FX expression of a fading US front-end premium versus CAD.
expression_comparison.rationale: Rates is cleaner. The discrepancy lives in the US policy path and US 2Y event overshoot, which SR3 marks directly. USDCAD is only modestly rich (5y z 0.99, 1m move z 1.23) and embeds 140bp of 2Y USD-over-CAD carry plus oil/BoC residuals, so it is a noisier, carry-opposed expression of the same US-rate view. AUDCAD at a 5y 99.96th percentile is a different stretch (AU housing vs CAD) and is not the same discrepancy.

context_build.causal_mechanism: After a fully priced 25bp hike, remaining front-end yield squeeze is the market still converting a known FOMC outcome plus an energy-shock narrative into extra 2027 hikes. Mean reversion requires that additive premium to fade once (i) the overnight benchmark has already jumped with the hike and (ii) the extreme oil-supply tail that justified more tightening is reduced. The trade tests whether Mar-27 SOFR implied (4.58) still needs ~three extra 25bp steps beyond the new 3.85 SOFR fixing, or whether that path was an overshoot around a known event.
context_build.path_to_current_price: Verified path: Reuters recorded >90% probability of a 25bp hike into the Sep-16 FOMC; the Fed delivered 25bp to 3.75–4.00%; NY Fed SOFR was 3.62 on 2026-09-16 and 3.85 on 2026-09-17; US 2Y as of 2026-09-18 is 476bp, 100th percentile of the 1y sample, +9bp 1d (z 1.90) and +57bp 1m (z 3.29); SR3 strip as of the funding/tradable layer is 4.00 (2026-09), 4.32 (2026-12), 4.58 (2027-03), 4.72 (2027-06), peaking at 4.755 (2027-09). US 2s10s as of 2026-09-17 is +56bp, 0.6th percentile 1y, -18bp over 1m—the curve footprint of the same front-end selloff. Desk last-24h thesis: energy shock is keeping term-rate pressure elevated even where domestic growth is softer, reinforced by BoJ +25bp to 1.25% and a 6–3 BoE hold with three hike votes.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known before the cutoff: August CPI had already kept a Fed tightening bias; the Sep-16 hike itself was >90% priced. New or newly transmitted: the hike actually printed and SOFR jumped 23bp into 3.85; Saudi ship-to-ship crude via Oman reduced the extreme oil-supply tail; US 2Y continued to 476bp / 100th percentile after the decision rather than giving back the event premium. A known hike cannot explain a new 1m 3.3-sigma 2Y squeeze unless the market is still adding an energy/global-tightening overlay on top of the already-priced 25bp.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: SR3H7 at 4.58 versus SOFR 3.85 prices about 73bp of additional tightening by Mar-27 (roughly three more 25bp steps). SR3M7 at 4.72 and SR3U7 at 4.755 extend that to ~87–90.5bp by mid/late 2027. The sovereign 2Y at 4.76 is consistent with that 12m implied peak. Price therefore requires that US inflation/labor stay hot enough, and the energy shock persist enough, to deliver a multi-hike cycle after Sep-16—not a one-and-done.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: Disagree that the residual 73bp of Mar-27 hike premium is still required now that the Sep hike is in the overnight fixing and the extreme oil-supply tail has been reduced. The disagreement is not that the Fed has become dovish, nor that US gauges are weak; it is that the post-decision front end overshot a known 25bp by converting a fading oil tail and global hawkish headlines into extra 2027 hikes.
context_build.price_decomposition: Level versus change: overnight SOFR 3.85 is the new policy floor (level); the 1m +57bp in US 2Y and the +73bp SR3H7-over-SOFR spread are the change/premium. Tenor: the mispricing is in 1H27 SOFR (Dec-26 4.32 already contains the next hike; Mar-27 4.58 and Jun-27 4.72 are the additive steps). Curve: 2s10s flattened 18bp over 1m to a 1y extreme, so the marginal driver is the front end, not a parallel long-end term-premium shock. Cross-market: CA 2Y 327bp (98th percentile 1y) fell 8bp on the latest CA observation while US 2Y rose 9bp, so the squeeze is US-led rather than a uniform G10 hike. AU 2Y 499.9bp (99th percentile) is a separate housing/inflation story, not this trade.

historical_reference.distribution: US 2Y 476bp sits at the 100th percentile of the packet 1y (n=252) distribution with z 2.89; the 1m change of +57bp has z 3.29 on that same 1y change distribution. US 2s10s +56bp is the 0.6th percentile 1y (z -2.00) after a -18bp 1m flattening, but only the 65.5th percentile over 5y—so the curve extreme is a 1y-window fact, not a 5y inversion. CA-US 2Y at -140bp is the 3.8th/4.3rd percentile (1y/5y) and is cited as a discovery contrast: Canada is historically cheap versus the US because overnight CORRA 2.29 versus SOFR 3.85 already anchors a ~156bp policy gap, so that spread extreme is not this fade.
analogs: Closest supplied analog set is US 2s10s 1m flattening of -18bp (2026-09-17). 2024-02-26: level -71bp, prior 1m -18, forward 1m +4bp / 3m +7bp (modest subsequent steepening from a deeply inverted starting point). 2022-04-08: level +20bp, prior 1m -18, forward 1m +13bp / 3m -21bp (1m steepening then 3m re-flattening). 2022-12-14: level -91bp, prior 1m -18, forward 1m +20bp / 3m +14bp (steepened). 2023-05-30: level -99bp, prior 1m -18, forward 1m -31bp / 3m -11bp (kept flattening). Two of four same-pace flattenings steepened in the next month; one kept flattening hard. The packet does not attach named historical_move_analogs directly to the US_2Y +57bp 1m level series; that absence is explicit.

Secondary analog on the related CA-US 2Y 1m move of -17bp: 2025-01-30 at almost the same spread level (-145bp) then forward 1m -5bp / 3m +25bp (spread mean-reverted over a quarter). 2024-12-18 at -130bp then 1m -3 / 3m -20 (spread cheapened further). Mixed, so the CA-US screen is not used as the trade.
historical_reference.regime_differences: The 2022–23 2s10s analogs were often already inverted (levels -71 to -99bp) during a still-early hiking cycle with inflation far above target; today's 2s10s is positively sloped at +56bp after a 25bp hike that was >90% priced and with Core PCE described in the retained US inflation gauge as only modestly hotter than policy-neutral (Jul-26 +0.2% m/m). Aug-26 unemployment 4.1% unchanged, AHE +0.3% m/m / +3.1% y/y, payrolls +162k. BoJ has just hiked to a 31-year high 1.25% and BoE split 6–3, a more globally hawkish overlay than several 2024 analog dates. Energy-shock plumbing (pipeline attack then Saudi STS workaround) has no clean one-for-one match in those 2s10s episodes. Therefore analogs support only a partial front-end giveback, not a full unwind to pre-hike SOFR 3.62.

independent_checks: Policy path (SOFR/SR3): overnight 3.85; Dec-26 4.32 (+47bp); Mar-27 4.58 (+73bp); Jun-27 4.72 (+87bp); Sep-27 4.755 (+90.5bp). The Mar-27 contract is the cleanest single mark of leftover hikes after Sep.
Sovereign US 2Y: 476bp, 100th percentile 1y, 1m +57bp z 3.29, as of 2026-09-18—same direction as SR3, different dataset (Treasury vs futures).
US 2s10s: +56bp, 0.6th percentile 1y, 1m -18bp, as of 2026-09-17—curve confirmation that the selloff is front-end led.

Temperature gauges (retained dashboard_v8 plus hard inputs as of 2026-09-17): US inflation 72, labor 75, activity 69, consumer 74. This check argues AGAINST an aggressive dove fade and caps size/confidence: data are still hot, so the thesis is event-premium mean reversion, not a growth-break.

Oil/news: Saudi STS workaround off Oman reduced the extreme supply tail (2026-09-16), while a separate rollup still warns that energy-market shock absorbers are weakening. That disagreement is preserved: tail reduced, residual energy risk remains.

Cross-market: CA labor 38 / consumer 45 / inflation 55 with core near 2% and CORRA only 2.29, yet CORRA still prices ~84bp by Mar-27 and ~136bp to a ~3.65 terminal. That is the same energy-hawk overlay in Canada, but the overnight gap versus SOFR is an anchor, so Canada is triangulation not the expression.
context_build.flow_and_positioning_check: CME_positioning is unavailable in the frozen packet; no SR3/Treasury futures ownership print exists. CFTC TFF as of 2026-09-15 is FX-only and partial. CAD leveraged funds are net short CAD (-39,022 contracts, -10.9% of OI) but that net is the 99th percentile 1y / z 1y +2.12 with a +16,426 weekly cover, so CAD shorts are not a crowded extreme. AUD open interest is a 99th percentile 1y/3y fact and is relevant to an AUD fade, not to SOFR. Inference: the US 2Y spike cannot be attributed to documented CTA/levered rates liquidation. Unknown: dealer SR3 or UST futures positioning. Do not treat plumbing as the explanation; also do not claim the front end is proven crowded in futures.

policy_path_check.pricing_summary: US: NY Fed SOFR 3.85 as of 2026-09-17 after a 23bp jump from 3.62 on 2026-09-16, consistent with the delivered 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00%. CME SR3 implieds: 2026-09 4.00 (+15bp), 2026-12 4.32 (+47bp), 2027-03 4.58 (+73bp), 2027-06 4.72 (+87bp), 2027-09 4.755 (+90.5bp), then a gentle decline through 2028. Funding_context maps those 3m/6m/12m points to SR3Z6/SR3H7/SR3U7. Canada and Australia paths are available but are not the selected expression: CORRA 2.29 with +84bp by Mar-27; AONIA 4.35 with +51bp by Mar-27. NZ policy path/rates are unavailable (RBNZ B2 HTTP 403).
policy_path_check.rationale: A short-dated US rates idea must be anchored in the live SOFR/SR3 path, not in the US 2Y percentile. The 2Y at 476bp is the discovery screen; SR3H7 at 4.58 is the tradable statement of leftover hikes. Policy-path status is ok for US in the frozen packet, so the expression is SOFR_2027-03 rather than a sovereign 2Y substitute.

trade.structure: Long CME SR3H7, paper alias SOFR_2027-03, marked in implied-rate space (100 minus futures price). Packet mid implied_rate 4.58 / price 95.42 from funding_context.sr3 and tradable_rate_curves. Side long is long duration (P&L inverted in implied-rate space). Single-contract family locked to SOFR; no migration onto CORRA/AONIA or Treasuries.
trade.thesis: VERIFIED: Sep-16 FOMC hike 25bp to 3.75–4.00% was >90% priced into the decision; SOFR printed 3.85 on 2026-09-17 versus 3.62 the prior session; US 2Y 476bp is the 100th percentile 1y after a +57bp 1m change (z 3.29); SR3H7 implies 4.58, +73bp over SOFR; Saudi STS workaround reduced the extreme oil-supply tail; US inflation/labor gauges remain 72/75 with Aug unemployment 4.1% and payrolls +162k. INFERENCE: the residual Mar-27 hike premium is the crowded energy-hawk overlay described by the last-24h desk thesis, not the minimum path required by the delivered 25bp. A plausible normalization is a partial giveback of that overlay toward the already-priced Dec-26 implied 4.32, not a collapse to 3.85. UNKNOWN: CME SR3/UST positioning; whether August CPI's tightening bias plus still-hot gauges deliver the next 25bp inside the Dec-26 window. Sidecar open_positions is empty, so this is a new OPEN versus the $100m gross cap.
trade.mispricing: Mar-27 SOFR implied 4.58 still prices ~73bp of extra tightening after a hike that was already in the futures strip and is now in the overnight fixing, while the oil-supply tail that justified adding more hikes has been reduced. The 1m 3.3-sigma US 2Y squeeze is the screen; the mispricing is the leftover SR3 path, not the percentile itself.
why_now: The Sep-16 25bp hike has printed and SOFR has jumped to 3.85, so the known event is in the overnight benchmark rather than still ahead.
US 2Y continued to a 1y high (476bp, 100th percentile) after that known event instead of giving back event premium.
Saudi STS crude via Oman is a same-week reduction in the extreme oil-supply tail that was feeding the additive hawkish overlay.
SR3H7 remains +73bp over the new SOFR fixing, so the tradable path still embeds two-to-three extra hikes that the mean-reversion case says were over-extrapolated.
Paper book is flat (sidecar open_positions []) while the seat pays official SOFR 3.85 ACT/360 on the full $100m anyway; deploying 40m is a sized expression of a live, post-event discrepancy.
evidence_refs: rollup:August CPI keeps the Fed tightening bias intact
last24:BoJ raises its policy rate to 1.25%
trade.horizon: 4–8 weeks, through the Dec-26 SR3 window and the next US inflation/labor prints that can validate or kill leftover 1H27 hike premium
trade.entry: Packet mid only: SOFR_2027-03 / SR3H7 implied_rate 4.58 (price 95.42) from frozen funding_context.sr3 and tradable_rate_curves; as_of aligned to the 2026-09-17 SOFR/SR3 layer. No broker quote.
trade.target: Partial mean reversion of Mar-27 implied toward the packet Dec-26 SR3Z6 implied 4.32, fading the extra ~26bp of 1H27 premium after the delivered Sep hike. Not a target of overnight SOFR 3.85.
trade.invalidation: Thesis is wrong if the next 25bp is clearly re-armed and delivered into the Dec-26 SR3 window while SR3H7 implied holds at or above the packet Jun-27 mid 4.72, or if US labor/inflation hard inputs re-accelerate from the retained Aug-26/Jul-26 prints and the oil-supply tail re-widens. Wrong-timing, not wrong-thesis, if implied rates chop around 4.58 without a new hike signal; then extend horizon rather than add.
catalysts: Post-FOMC event-premium decay now that SOFR has printed 3.85.
Follow-through of the Saudi STS workaround into a softer energy-pass-through narrative versus the BoC/Fed energy-shock overlay.
US 2s10s mean-reverting some of the 1y-extreme 18bp 1m flattening as the front end cheapens versus 10s.
Next US inflation/labor prints that fail to escalate beyond the already-known modest-hot Core PCE and +162k payrolls.
principal_risks: US gauges are still hot (inflation 72, labor 75, consumer 74); August CPI already kept a tightening bias, so another 25bp can be delivered and SR3H7 can rally in yield.
Energy-market shock absorbers may still be weakening even if the extreme Saudi supply tail was reduced; a renewed oil spike re-justifies the hike path.
BoJ 1.25% and BoE 6–3 with three hike votes can keep a global hawkish term-rate bid that does not mean-revert on a US-only event fade.
CME positioning is missing; a still-under-positioned shorts-covering squeeze in UST/SR3 can extend the 2Y overshoot.
1-day as-of gap: US 2Y is 2026-09-18 versus SOFR/SR3 2026-09-17.
AUDCAD 5y extreme and AU housing are a separate stretch; not being in that trade is a missed-opportunity risk, not this book's risk.
